transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Time: 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orionis CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of Infra), Jared Mills (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Renewal check in; customer wants APAC burst capacity and short extension to align procurement calendar. Ask: validate latency in APAC, provide SOC2 and network diagram, provide pricing for add-on and pilot details.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, welcome. Maya from Redwood here, thanks for making time, how's it going in London, Priya?
[00:09] Priya Nair: Hey Maya, good thanks. Bit busy but excited to chat through this. Liam and Jared are with me.
[00:13] Liam O'Connor: Morning, all. Quick note, I might jump in with some infra specifics.
[00:18] Jared Mills: Hi, yeah, procurement on standby, want to understand timelines.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Today's goal — quick renewal touch, talk APAC edge/top-up options, and outline a private pilot to validate latency and cost. Lucas from our SE team will cover the benchmark plan.
[00:32] Lucas Ortega: Hi all. I'll run through what we typically measure. Also re: KV cache warm-up, continuous batching, stuff that affects p99 latency.

[02:05] Priya Nair: To be blunt: our product has a small but growing user base in APAC; we saw a spike in requests last quarter. We need low single-digit ms token latency for our real-time feature and can't afford user-visible hiccups. We're evaluating adding a regional edge or burst pool.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Understood. Right now you're on Hosted with a reserved commit in US/EU only — can you confirm current committed RUs? (audio glitch)
[02:34] Liam O'Connor: Sure, current commit is roughly 750k tokens/day equivalent, mostly US-west and EU-central. APAC traffic is ~12% right now but trending up.

[03:12] Priya Nair: We're asking for a short runway — a 6-month extension on our current contract so procurement can align, and a 30% uplift in capacity with an APAC add-on. Ideally on Dedicated or Private? We're open but want guarantees.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Thanks. A couple points — we can do an APAC edge add-on on Dedicated pools or stand up a Private VPC region depending on your security needs. There's also a light-weight APAC burst option (no full private control plane) that sits on our Dedicated fleet with region pinning, quicker to activate.

[04:05] Liam O'Connor: What's the difference in SLOs? I.e., if we go burst vs private, what latency guarantees do we get and does KV cache behavior differ?
[04:15] Lucas Ortega: Practically, Dedicated edge with a pinned pool gives consistent throughput and predictable p99s because the collocated KV cache is warm for your workload. Burst capacity has some cold-start variability and higher p95 during extreme spikes. Private (customer-managed VPC) gives you the most control but requires longer lead time and network setup.
[04:45] Priya Nair: For compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs. We do not want tokens to leave our tenancy for APAC if possible.
[04:55] Maya Chen: We can integrate KMS in both Private and Dedicated models; for Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for keys, and audit logs are standard. For full tenancy isolation and customer-controlled networking, Private is the path. But Private will add some onboarding weeks.

[06:10] Jared Mills: From procurement: if we do a 6-month extension, can pricing be prorated and include the APAC add-on as an amendment? We need to see an example amendment. Also any early termination or capacity rollback clauses we should know?
[06:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we typically do a contract amendment for short extensions to align calendars. We'll draft a 6-month amendment with an APAC add-on SKU and prorated billing. We can add a rollback clause with 30 days notice for non-committed burst capacity but not for reserved Dedicated pools.

[07:02] Lucas Ortega: On the technical side, for the pilot we propose: 1) small dedicated pool in APAC equivalent to 2x your existing APAC QPS for warmup, 2) run 48-72 hour steady-state test with synthetic and traffic-replay, 3) measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost; also run quantization profile to see token cost reductions.
[07:30] Priya Nair: That sounds reasonable. Do you support our internal cert team running pen-tests against the Private deploy?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Yes, we can support a pen-test on Private with coordination. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide SOC2 and our network diagrams; we prefer to handle certain infra-level checks through our security team.

[09:00] Liam O'Connor: Question: latency numbers — can you share historical p99 for similar customers from your APAC fleet? We need baseline.
[09:12] Lucas Ortega: I can share anonymized profiles — typical p99s for small seq-length gen on APAC Dedicated are 180-350 ms depending on model and batch size. If you target low-latency, we recommend sequence length tuning, batching windows, and sometimes a quantized model variant — which can shave 30-40% on cost but the impact on latency varies.

[12:05] Priya Nair: We're also sensitive to token usage growth — can Redwood provide telemetry per token-type? We want breakdown by prompt vs completion and embedding vs chat calls.
[12:18] Maya Chen: Yep — console provides token-level breakdown, cost per token, and route-level dashboards. We can include a sample dashboard export as part of the package.

[14:40] Jared Mills: Competitor question: we've had talks with AlpacaServe — they offered cheaper rates but with no SSO or enterprise audit logs. Is that consistent?
[14:50] Maya Chen: That aligns with what we see — cheaper commodity endpoints but without SLA/enterprise controls. CloudFoundry AI also offers a Managed model but they'd require you to manage your own KMS integration. We position Redwood for teams needing predictable economics + compliance.

[17:05] Lucas Ortega: Back to pilot specifics — we'll need a list of test prompts, a replay dataset, and a small traffic shaping plan. For KV cache warm-up we recommend a 24-hour warm-up window where we route 25% of production traffic to the pool. That minimizes cold p99 spikes.

[19:30] Priya Nair: Ok, timeline wise procurement wants things done by end of April. Can you commit to a pilot by the first week of April?
[19:40] Maya Chen: Roughly yes — if we get agreement and PO by March 24 we can have an APAC burst pool standing by for an April 6 start. Private would need more lead time (4-6 weeks after network handoff).

[22:10] Liam O'Connor: On the security front — KMS, SSO/SAML, RBAC — any gotchas for us? We use Azure AD for SSO and want SCIM for user provisioning.
[22:23] Lucas Ortega: We support SAML SSO via Azure AD and SCIM provisioning; for KMS we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via envelope encryption. For Private we can accept customer-managed VPC peering and egress restrictions.

[25:00] Priya Nair: Costs — if we add APAC Dedicated plus a 30% token uplift, what's the rough delta? We need a ballpark to present to finance.
[25:12] Maya Chen: Rough ballpark: APAC Dedicated delta is typically 18-28% on top of your current commit for the same token volume due to regional capacity and reserved pricing. With burst-only option it's ~10-15% as a premium. We'll send an itemized worksheet.

[28:40] Jared Mills: For the amendment, can you include an option to convert the 6-month extension into a 12-month at a reduced rate if we decide later?
[28:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we can include a conversion clause with a retroactive credit or a pre-negotiated price ladder. We'll show both options in the draft amendment.

[31:05] Lucas Ortega: A couple of technical caveats: if you use aggressive quantization we need to run quality checks on your eval set — sometimes completion quality drops on certain instruction patterns. We'll include a short eval pass as part of the pilot.

[33:20] Priya Nair: Good. Who will own the benchmark run on our side? Liam?
[33:28] Liam O'Connor: Yep I can run the replay and join Lucas for validation. Need a test harness sample.

[35:55] Maya Chen: Action recap — Maya to send pricing + amendment sample, Lucas to share pilot plan and benchmarking checklist, Priya to share QPS and token distribution, Jared to confirm procurement timeline.

[38:10] Jared Mills: We'll want to see a draft SOW or pilot scope doc before committing.
[38:17] Maya Chen: We'll include that with the pilot plan.

[40:00] Priya Nair: A couple of nitty-gritty items: data retention, log redaction, and how long audit logs are kept.
[40:10] Lucas Ortega: Audit logs retention configurable — default 90 days in hosted, longer with add-on. For Private you control retention. We support log redaction on PII fields in the console.

[43:30] Liam O'Connor: Networking — if we go Private we need a simple network diagram to share with our security team.
[43:38] Maya Chen: We'll attach a network diagram and shepherd it through our security contact.

[46:05] Priya Nair: Sounding good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[46:11] Maya Chen: None on our side. Need the PO and the QPS numbers to lock dates.

[48:50] Jared Mills: Procurement will aim for March 24 for PO; that's the internal target. If we miss that the April pilot will slip.

[50:00] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize the amendment draft and the pricing worksheet and get them over by Monday. Lucas will follow up on the pilot plan.

[51:00] Priya Nair: Thanks all. Excited to try this.
[51:05] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artefacts — product name rendered as "Redwood Dedecate" in parts of the AI notes. References to continuous batching referred as "continual batching" in a couple spots.
